newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Rand Refinery already selling gold direct.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Rand Refinery already selling gold direct.

text.p: South Africa's Rand Refinery said on Friday it was already marketing gold direct on behalf of producers and had in 1996 sold and exported 140 tonnes direct.

Commenting on news that Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd had received Reserve Bank approval to market internationally a third of its own output, it said this represented a reallocation to Harmony of its share of gold already sold direct by the Rand Refinery.

"What Harmony has achieved is the reallocation to their company of their proportion of directly marketed gold already undertaken by the industry through the Rand Refinery," Rand Refinery said in a statement.
"This means that gold sold and marketed by Harmony will not constitute any additional foreign exchange gain, being simply an offset against business done already by the Rand Refinery."
The refinery said the Reserve Bank approval stipulated that the sales should be in the form of gold products of one kilogramme bars or less.
At present all South Africa's mines refine their gold at the Rand Refinery -- the world's biggest -- which is collectively owned by the industry.
But Harmony announced last year that it planned to break ranks by establishing its own commercial-scale gold refinery, which should be completed in the third quarter of 1997.
The mine said it hoped it would eventually be allowed to market direct its full production of around 24 tonnes a year.
